1978.notes: Computed from the statute's indexing (Stats. 1978, ch. 569) as the California Franchise Tax Board's annual reports describe it (microfilm scans on archive.org): the 1977 schedule (FTB Table 1B; joint brackets twice the single ones, income splitting) with every bracket widened each year by that year's index factor, 5.222% for 1978, 6.88% for 1979, 17.33% for 1980, 8.26% for 1981 and 9.32% for 1982 (FTB 1982 Annual Report, Table 1A footnote 7; the 1982 factor from the 1983 Annual Report, micro_IA40706918_0345), and rounded to the nearest $10 each year. The standard deduction was indexed from 1979 by the full June-to-June California CPI change (the bracket factor plus the 3% threshold removed: 9.88% for 1979; FTB 1980 and 1981 reports), also rounded to $10. Checks against amounts the reports print: the top (11%) joint bracket starts at $44,280 for 1981 (FTB 1982 report, 'Indexing') and $48,400 for 1982 (1983 report); the joint standard deduction is $2,800 for 1981 (1982 report) and $1,530 single / $3,060 joint for 1982 (1983 report, 'Deductions'); every computed value matches. The lower brackets weren't printed for these years, so they rest on the same indexing rule. Personal and dependent exemption credits (indexed too; quadrupled one time for 1978) are tax credits, not modelled.

1983.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism, Table 48 (State Individual Income Tax Rates for 1983, as of December 1983; printed p. 62) prints the California schedule for joint taxpayers and surviving spouses as indexed for 1983 ($0-$3,020 no tax, 1% to $9,200 ... 11% over $50,860) and says single taxpayers and married persons filing separately pay 1% on taxable income between $1,511 and $4,600 and 11% over $25,431; Table 47 (as of October 1, 1983; p. 60) gives the single brackets as $4,600 lowest / $25,430 highest and the zero bracket amount as $1,510 single / $3,020 joint. The single schedule recorded here is the printed joint schedule halved (joint tax is twice the tax on half the income, R&TC 17045, as the FTB annual reports' synopsis footnote states; every halved amount is a multiple of 10), with its printed endpoints $1,510, $4,600 and $25,430 matching; the intermediate single edges are not printed anywhere. FTB 1984 Annual Report (archive.org micro_IA40706922_0001) confirms the 1983 zero bracket amount $1,510/$3,020, the 1983 index factor -1.2% and the joint 11% threshold $50,860. Zero bracket amount is modelled as the 0% first bracket, so no deduction is recorded (itemizers deducted only the excess). Personal exemption credits ($38 per person / $76 joint) are tax credits, not modelled.

1984.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism, Table 53 (State Individual Income Tax Rates for 1984, as of December 1984; printed p. 75): California single and married-filing-separately schedule as indexed for 1984 ($0-$1,580 no tax, 1% $1,581-$4,810 ... 11% over $26,600); the table says that for joint returns the tax is twice the amount it would be if taxable income were cut in half, so the joint schedule is recorded as double the single one. Table 52 (as of November 1984; p. 73) gives the zero bracket amount as $1,580 single / $3,160 joint. FTB 1985 Annual Report (archive.org micro_IA40706925_0099) confirms: 1984 inflation factor 4.6%, zero bracket amount $1,580/$3,160, joint maximum-rate threshold $53,200 (= 2 x $26,600). Zero bracket amount is modelled as the 0% first bracket, so no deduction is recorded. Personal exemption credits ($40 per person / $80 joint) are tax credits, not modelled.

1985.notes: Computed: the 1984 indexed schedule (this file's 1984 entry: ACIR 1984 ed. Table 53, confirmed by the FTB 1985 Annual Report) multiplied by 1.046 and rounded to the nearest $10. The California Franchise Tax Board 1987 Annual Report (archive.org micro_IA40706931_0296; history-of-rates table footnote) gives the bracket indexing rates as 4.6% for 1984, 4.6% for 1985 and 3.5% for 1986, and its narrative gives the 1986 inflation factor as 3.5% with a $1,710 zero bracket amount. Check: these 1985 brackets multiplied by 1.035 and rounded to the nearest $10 reproduce all eleven published 1986 brackets (this file's 1986 entry, FTB 1992 Annual Report tables) exactly, while a 3.5% factor for 1985 reproduces none. The FTB 1986 Annual Report (micro_IA40706928_0205) states a 3.5% factor, a $1,710 zero bracket amount, $86 joint personal credits and a $57,580 joint maximum-rate threshold 'for the 1985 taxable year'; those are the 1986 amounts given by the 1987 report and the 1986 schedule ($1,710 is 8.2% above the 1984 $1,580, not 3.5%), and its own footnote lists 3.5% as the last factor, so they were not used. Zero bracket amount (0% first bracket) $1,650 single; joint schedule = double the single one, as in the 1984 and 1986 entries (joint maximum-rate threshold $55,640). Personal exemption credits are tax credits, not modelled.

1986.notes: FTB tax rate schedules for taxable year 1986 from the California Franchise Tax Board 1992 Annual Report (microfilm scan on archive.org), Personal Income Tax Synopsis of Tax Rates, Table 1A (married filing jointly) and Table 1B (single and married filing separately), "Taxable Year 1986" column (page 44 of the report; the same column is printed in the 1988, 1989, 1990 and 1991 annual reports). Indexed amounts as printed; in 1984-1986 the standard deduction was a zero bracket amount built into the schedule as the 0% first bracket ($1,710 single / $3,420 joint, confirmed by the FTB 1987 Annual Report, which also says the 1986 inflation factor was 3.5%), so no deduction is recorded (itemizers deducted only the excess over the zero bracket amount). The 1987 Annual Report narrative gives the 1986 joint maximum-rate threshold as $57,590, $10 more than the $57,580 printed in the tables; the table figure is used. Personal exemption credits ($43 per person / $86 joint in 1986) are tax credits, not modelled.
